view.label: References
view.description: System and technology decisions, trade-offs, alternatives and typed relationships.

disclaimer: Curated architectural evaluations; alternatives are comparisons, not installed or selected components. Package declarations and configuration are not proof of working production features.

systems.why: Interactive manipulation must feel immediate without turning speculative previews into accepted state.
strengths: Fast user feedback independent of slow exact solvers
Human and agent changes can use a common semantic operation boundary
weaknesses: Previews can diverge from authoritative results
Requires explicit stale/candidate presentation

alternatives.name: Direct model mutation
alternatives.tradeoff: Simpler initially, but creates unsafe hidden state changes

alternatives.name: CAD command stack
alternatives.tradeoff: Familiar interactions; correctness still requires transaction boundaries

systems.why: Separate probabilistic reasoning from deterministic world authority.
strengths: Can explore alternatives and critique decisions
Swappable model providers behind bounded interfaces
weaknesses: Proposals can be incorrect or underspecified
Context, tools and permissions require strict governance

alternatives.name: Autonomous agent writes
alternatives.tradeoff: Fewer approval steps but unacceptable mutation and audit risks

alternatives.name: Single assistant prompt
alternatives.tradeoff: Lower orchestration cost but weaker specialist verification

systems.why: Keep semantic building truth, identity, revisions and evidence in one governed place.
strengths: Transactions enable provenance and stable references
weaknesses: Complex state model and migration work
Concurrency and failure policies must be rigorously tested

alternatives.name: Document-centric BIM database
alternatives.tradeoff: Mature and familiar but can couple geometry and authority

alternatives.name: Event-sourced graph store
alternatives.tradeoff: Natural history and relations, but additional operational complexity

systems.why: Generate candidate precise geometry without letting a particular kernel define semantic truth.
strengths: Exact and approximate strategies can be selected per task
weaknesses: Topology naming and tolerance handling are difficult
Expensive solves require fallbacks and timeouts

alternatives.name: CGAL
alternatives.tradeoff: Strong computational geometry; different B-rep/CAD integration trade-offs

alternatives.name: Parasolid
alternatives.tradeoff: Mature commercial CAD kernel with licensing and distribution implications

systems.why: Evaluate whether a candidate world satisfies technical and policy invariants before acceptance.
strengths: Policies can be tested independently from render code
weaknesses: Regulations can be ambiguous or version-dependent
Cross-domain constraints can be computationally expensive

alternatives.name: Hard-coded UI checks
alternatives.tradeoff: Quick prototyping but inconsistent enforcement

alternatives.name: External rule engine
alternatives.tradeoff: Powerful declarative policies with integration overhead

systems.why: Derive meshes, viewports, drawings and schedules from revisioned semantic state.
strengths: One model can support many purpose-specific views
Derived artifacts can be discarded and regenerated
weaknesses: Invalidation and cache freshness add complexity
Mesh detail cannot replace authoritative building semantics

alternatives.name: Single geometry-first scene graph
alternatives.tradeoff: Simple interactive renderer but difficult for robust documentation

alternatives.name: Full independent drawing model
alternatives.tradeoff: Flexible drafting but risks disconnected truth

systems.why: Keep regulations, analysis services, importers and fabrication adapters replaceable.
strengths: Third-party systems cannot silently own world state
weaknesses: Version and schema mismatches require careful translation
External data quality and provenance vary

alternatives.name: Direct vendor integration
alternatives.tradeoff: Less boilerplate but high coupling

alternatives.name: Universal exchange format alone
alternatives.tradeoff: Interoperable files but incomplete semantic operations

systems.why: Reserve sensitivity-guided computation as optional advice, not as an exact authority shortcut.
strengths: Useful for local previews and optimization proposals
weaknesses: Gradients fail around discontinuities
Requires trust radii, uncertainty and exact fallbacks

alternatives.name: Finite differences
alternatives.tradeoff: Simple to apply, but potentially costly and noisy

alternatives.name: Full exact solve per proposal
alternatives.tradeoff: Higher authority but slower interactive feedback

systems.why: Make authored view, sheet and annotation intent persistent while deriving scale-specific graphics.
strengths: Model-linked details can remain revision coherent
Issue packages can be validated and immutable
weaknesses: Scale-specific simplification is difficult
Anchors and approved overrides require careful lifecycle management

alternatives.name: Independent 2D CAD drafting
alternatives.tradeoff: Flexible detail work but difficult automatic coordination

alternatives.name: BIM-only 3D cut views
alternatives.tradeoff: Coherent geometry but insufficient drawing abstraction at every scale

systems.why: Compare project-grounded alternatives while preserving context, constraints and documentary coherence.
strengths: Cross-view continuity checks can expose unnoticed drift
weaknesses: Learned suggestions can hallucinate details
Requires strong source attribution and human sign-off

alternatives.name: Manual drawing audits
alternatives.tradeoff: Reliable human judgement but slow and hard to reproduce

alternatives.name: Unconstrained generative correction
alternatives.tradeoff: Fast variants but can silently break intent

technologies.name: TypeScript
technologies.what: Statically typed JavaScript used for the monorepo's domain models, services and browser applications.
technologies.why: One shared implementation language across contracts, front end and adapters.
strengths: Strong editor tooling and typed interfaces
weaknesses: Types vanish at runtime
Large generics and build graphs can be complex

alternatives.name: Rust
alternatives.tradeoff: Stronger memory-safety/performance potential but greater implementation and interop cost

alternatives.name: Plain JavaScript
alternatives.tradeoff: Lighter tooling but fewer compile-time guarantees

technologies.name: pnpm
technologies.what: Node package manager supporting workspace linking and efficient dependency installation.
technologies.why: Single lockfile and shared local packages in the monorepo.
weaknesses: Requires Node tooling discipline
Workspace dependency drift still needs CI

alternatives.name: npm workspaces
alternatives.tradeoff: Ubiquitous, simpler defaults; different performance and lockfile semantics

alternatives.name: Yarn
alternatives.tradeoff: Comparable workspace management with different configuration choices

technologies.name: Turborepo
technologies.what: Task graph runner for builds, linting and tests across interdependent packages.
technologies.why: Coordinates monorepo verification without manually scripting every package.
weaknesses: Cache correctness needs attention
Build graph complexity can hide failed edges

alternatives.name: Nx
alternatives.tradeoff: Richer project graph and tooling with greater framework complexity

alternatives.name: Plain scripts
alternatives.tradeoff: Transparent but less scalable for dependency orchestration

technologies.name: Vitest
technologies.what: JavaScript and TypeScript test runner integrated into project packages.
technologies.why: Make contract and regression checks runnable in CI.
weaknesses: Benchmark results depend on environment
Integration and browser tests need other tools

alternatives.name: Jest
alternatives.tradeoff: Large ecosystem but more configuration in modern ESM stacks

alternatives.name: Node test runner
alternatives.tradeoff: Fewer dependencies, more limited built-in ecosystem

technologies.name: Zod
technologies.what: Runtime schema parsing and validation for TypeScript data boundaries.
technologies.why: Validate input and serialized domain contracts where static types are insufficient.
weaknesses: Parsing large payloads has measurable cost
Schemas do not prove engineering correctness

alternatives.name: JSON Schema/Ajv
alternatives.tradeoff: Interoperable schemas; separate type synchronization

alternatives.name: Valibot
alternatives.tradeoff: Modular validation footprint with different API trade-offs

technologies.name: React
technologies.what: Component-based user interface library for the designer application.
technologies.why: Supports composable inspection, editing and workbench views.
weaknesses: Complex state synchronization can cause bugs
Not a geometry kernel or state authority

alternatives.name: Vue
alternatives.tradeoff: Approachable reactive component model

alternatives.name: Svelte
alternatives.tradeoff: Compile-time approach with distinct ecosystem trade-offs

technologies.name: Vite
technologies.what: Browser development server and bundling tool.
technologies.why: Keep the designer app's development and build feedback fast.
weaknesses: Build and runtime configurations can diverge
Does not manage backend deployment

alternatives.name: Webpack
alternatives.tradeoff: Mature configurability with more setup

alternatives.name: Rspack
alternatives.tradeoff: Fast bundler with ecosystem compatibility considerations

technologies.name: Three.js
technologies.why: Render interactive derived models while semantic state lives elsewhere.
strengths: Good support for selection, camera and mesh workflows
weaknesses: Not an exact CAD solid modeller
Large scenes require careful draw-call and memory management

alternatives.name: Babylon.js
alternatives.tradeoff: Integrated real-time engine and tooling

alternatives.name: Custom WebGPU renderer
alternatives.tradeoff: Fine control but higher maintenance cost

technologies.name: OpenCascade / OCCT
technologies.what: Boundary-representation solid modelling kernel accessed through a dedicated geometry service.
technologies.why: Precise CAD operations behind engine-neutral contracts for reusable semantics.
strengths: Exact solid modelling and topology operations
Open-source kernel with broad CAD file ecosystem
weaknesses: Topology naming and numerical tolerances are difficult
WASM/native packaging and worker isolation are nontrivial

alternatives.name: Parasolid
alternatives.tradeoff: Commercial solid kernel with licensing and distribution trade-offs

alternatives.name: CGAL
alternatives.tradeoff: Powerful geometry algorithms, not a drop-in full CAD B-rep replacement

technologies.name: Fastify
technologies.what: Node.js HTTP server framework used by API and geometry services.
technologies.why: Keep service boundaries small with explicit request validation and error handling.
weaknesses: Requires disciplined schema and authentication design
Not a persistence or orchestration layer

alternatives.name: Express
alternatives.tradeoff: Simpler ubiquity with different type/performance characteristics

alternatives.name: NestJS
alternatives.tradeoff: Batteries-included modular architecture with more framework weight

technologies.name: PostgreSQL
technologies.what: Relational database configured in Docker Compose for application persistence.
technologies.why: Persist governed revisions, entities and transactional application records.
weaknesses: Graph traversals may need explicit indexes/models
Schema migration and database operations require care

alternatives.name: Neo4j
alternatives.tradeoff: Native graph traversal model but added consistency/operational concerns

alternatives.name: SQLite
alternatives.tradeoff: Very simple deployments with different concurrency/scaling envelope

technologies.name: Drizzle ORM
technologies.what: TypeScript-friendly object-relational mapping and SQL schema tooling.
technologies.why: Keep database access close to typed application models.
weaknesses: Migrations require governance
Not a substitute for domain transaction invariants

alternatives.name: Prisma
alternatives.tradeoff: Higher-level ORM/tooling with different query control

alternatives.name: Kysely
alternatives.tradeoff: Typed SQL builder with less ORM schema machinery

technologies.name: MinIO
technologies.what: S3-compatible object storage service present in the Docker Compose stack.
technologies.why: Store generated geometry and documents separately from authoritative relational metadata.
strengths: Object storage suited to large binary artifacts
weaknesses: Durability requires correct deployment settings
Object storage does not enforce semantic revision coherence

alternatives.name: AWS S3
alternatives.tradeoff: Managed storage and scale; cloud cost and dependency

alternatives.name: Filesystem
alternatives.tradeoff: Simple local storage, harder multi-worker coordination

technologies.name: Docker Compose
technologies.what: Container orchestration configuration for PostgreSQL, MinIO, geometry and optional meshing service.
weaknesses: Resource use and build overhead
Development compose is not production orchestration

alternatives.name: Kubernetes
alternatives.tradeoff: Scalable production orchestration with significantly higher complexity

alternatives.name: Local processes
alternatives.tradeoff: Faster debugging but less environment isolation

technologies.name: Gmsh
technologies.what: Meshing software offered as an optional container profile.
technologies.why: Provide mesh generation for analysis and specialist geometric workflows.
weaknesses: Mesh quality depends on source geometry
Not authoritative for semantic B-rep state

alternatives.name: TetGen
alternatives.tradeoff: Specialist tetrahedral meshing with different feature envelope

alternatives.name: Netgen
alternatives.tradeoff: Alternative open meshing toolkit

technologies.name: Playwright
technologies.what: Automated real-browser interaction testing used by Atlas smoke workflow.
technologies.why: Verify navigation, responsive behaviour and inspector UI beyond schema checks.
weaknesses: Tests can be timing-sensitive
Requires browser downloads and CI maintenance

alternatives.name: Cypress
alternatives.tradeoff: Alternative browser E2E framework with different architecture

alternatives.name: Pure unit tests
alternatives.tradeoff: Cheaper but cannot verify user-visible navigation
